title: Rumor:  Razor Lake gets 12 P-core only die with bLLC on Intel 18A-P
author: S
text:
Xebec
Well-known member

Razor Lake is the successor to Nova Lake, and will span both desktop and laptop segments.

This rumor is noteable because it means that they're making a high end variant of Razor Lake on 18A-P (high "per thread" performance requirement, with "enough" cores). This contrasts with Nova Lake where the expected highest end SKUs will/may be exclusive to TSMC N2P. Razor Lake will also have N2(P?) variants, as well, and goes on (retail) sale in 2028.

..

Source: https://videocardz.com/newz/intel-r...s-12-p-core-only-die-with-bllc-on-intel-18a-p

Intel is reportedly preparing an unlocked Razor Lake desktop processor featuring 12 P-cores on a single compute die. According to hardware leaker Jaykihn, the processor will use Intel’s 18A-P manufacturing process and feature bLLC (Big Last Level Cache). This would be a different design from the...

Jaykihn reports that the processor has a 12+0+4 configuration, consisting of 12 performance cores, no standard efficiency cores and four low-power efficiency cores. The 12 P-cores reportedly use the Coyote Cove architecture, which Intel is also expected to introduce with Nova Lake.

The leaker clarified that this is a dedicated P-core-only compute die, rather than a hybrid design with disabled E-cores. He also confirmed that all 12 P-cores reside on a single die, rather than two compute tiles with six P-cores each. The processor is reportedly unlocked and includes bLLC,...
